gaps.sentence: He demands ___ answer before the end of the day.
The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
gaps.explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
gaps.explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: He is ___ most experienced teacher in the school.
gaps.explanation: Superlative + of/in-phrase: the most experienced teacher in the school.

gaps.sentence: We're going to ___ Algarve for a fortnight in June.
gaps.explanation: Region names often take the: the Algarve, the Riviera.

gaps.sentence: ___ sun sets much later in summer.
gaps.explanation: 'The sun' — there is only one, so the definite article is used.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.
